analysis: Documentation-only PR; no source code in the supplied evidence. Changes: (1) hardware-requirements.md adds GLM-5.3-Flash gating (M5 Max/Ultra, >=256 GB, runtime capability glm5_next_v1, MTP required). (2) configuration.md adds a Local GLM qualification section: DARKBLOOM_EXPERIMENTAL_GLM5_NEXT (absolute path to a JSON selection file, max 4 MiB, process-local, not forwarded to launchd, ignored in coordinator mode). It pins the catalog/manifest to EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp via expectedAggregateSHA256, the chat template hash, and managed-loader byte verification (relevant to A-004, T-012, T-027). Adds DARKBLOOM_GLM_PERSISTENT_WIRED_RESIDENCY (forwarded to launchd; acceleration only, not admission) and DARKBLOOM_GLM_RECTANGULAR_VERIFY. Adds GLM load-fault gauges on the local /metrics endpoint and describes retained-fault semantics, which relate to availability (T-029). Adds GLM encrypted SSD prefix store default-on (T-041 scope; the T-041 'default-on' text for CBv2 models is consistent). (3) Weight hashing now first reads through a page-aligned F_NOCACHE descriptor (hashSingleFileUncached). Not verifiable from the supplied docs, but a read-then-load TOCTOU concern is unchanged. (4) New DEBUG-only DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE replaces the SE/Keychain KEK; the one finding above covers the threat-model gap. Unverified: source for SSDDebugCacheKeyFile.swift, the compile-out in release builds, GLM5NextLocalQualification validation, and whether the launchd passthrough list really matches the claims. Recommend that later passes confirm those if source appears.

findings.detail: This PR documents `DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE`. It replaces the Secure Enclave/Keychain-rooted SSD cache KEK with one derived from an operator-created plaintext file, and the result is reported as persistent. T-041 treats the Secure Enclave-rooted KEK as the root of AES-GCM wrapping, of the K_lookup HMAC names, and of the KEK-wipe purge. A file-held KEK removes that hardware root for any build that has the path. The doc says release builds do not compile the path, and it requires mode 0600, a single link and a non-symlink final component. The supplied evidence cannot confirm either the compile-time exclusion or the file checks, because only documentation changed. T-041 mitigations and detection_hint do not mention this override. Suggested fix: add the DEBUG-only file-KEK path to T-041 and TB-003 (file path: SSDDebugCacheKeyFile.swift; the compile-out guard); add a release-build test that the symbol is absent. Also record that KEK destruction is no longer a cryptographic purge when the key lives in a file.
findings.title: Threat model lacks coverage for the new DEBUG-only SSD cache KEK-from-file override
